final.answer: The valve operated by loop FIC-106-2 is FV-106-2, a globe control valve. Per its datasheet (Fisher ET/D100022X012), the valve plug seal (seal ring in the plug) is available in several materials. For the 2-piece valve plug seal (standard for NPS 1-6 valves except those with Cavitrol III cage): carbon-filled PTFE from -73 to 232 °C (-100 to 450 °F); ethylene-propylene from -40 to 232 °C (-40 to 450 °F, good with hot water/steam and most fire-resistant hydraulic oils but not petroleum-based fluids and other hydrocarbons); fluorocarbon from -18 to 204 °C (0 to 400 °F, for high-temperature air, hydrocarbons and certain other chemicals and solvents, not for steam or ammonia, not recommended for water above 82 °C/180 °F); and nitrile from -40 to 71 °C (-40 to 160 °F) for air and hydrocarbons or -40 to 82 °C (-40 to 180 °F) for other compatible fluids, but not with fire-resistant hydraulic oils. For the spring-loaded valve plug seal (standard for the NPS 8 valve and all NPS 1-6 valves with Cavitrol III cages, optional otherwise): PTFE with an N10276 spring from -73 to 232 °C (-100 to 450 °F), or PTFE/graphite with an R30003 spring from -73 to 316 °C (-100 to 600 °F), though limited to 260 °C/500 °F in oxidizing service — this is the extended-temperature version (with PEEK anti-extrusion rings: 316 °C/600 °F non-oxidizing, 260 °C/500 °F oxidizing). Other listed parts, such as stainless steel seal ring parts, PEEK anti-extrusion rings and PTFE V-ring packing (-40 to 232 °C / -40 to 450 °F), are noted as not limiting temperature, with other valve parts setting the limits instead. No part explicitly called a piston ring appears in the datasheet.
